original_value: Natural disasters are phenomena that can occur in any part of the world. They can cause massive amounts of destruction and leave entire cities in great need of assistance. The ability to quickly and accurately deliver aid to impacted areas is crucial toward not only saving time and money, but, most importantly, lives. We present a deep learning-based computer vision model to semantically infer the magnitude of damage to individual buildings after natural disasters using pre- and post-disaster satellite images. This model helps alleviate a major bottleneck in disaster management decision support by automating the analysis of the magnitude of damage to buildings post-disaster. In this paper, we will show our methods and results for how we were able to obtain a better performance than existing models, especially in moderate to significant magnitudes of damage, along with ablation studies to show our methods and results for the importance and impact of different training parameters in deep learning for satellite imagery. We were able to obtain an overall F1 score of 0.868 with our methods.

result.paraphrase: Natural disasters can happen anywhere in the world and may cause widespread devastation, leaving whole cities in urgent need of aid. Rapid and accurate delivery of assistance to affected areas is essential for saving time and money, and above all, lives. We present a deep learning computer vision model that semantically infers the extent of damage to individual buildings after natural disasters from pre- and post-disaster satellite imagery. By automating post-disaster building damage analysis, this model helps relieve a major bottleneck in disaster-management decision support. In this paper, we present our methods and results, showing improved performance over existing models, particularly for moderate to severe damage, and include ablation studies demonstrating the importance and impact of different deep learning training parameters for satellite imagery. Using our methods, we achieved an overall F1 score of 0.868.
